newsitem.title: USA: Ind. governor floats plan for Chicago skyway tolls.
newsitem.headline: Ind. governor floats plan for Chicago skyway tolls.

text.p: - Indiana Gov. Frank O'Bannon has floated an idea for easing congestion on a state freeway in the northwest part of the state -- temporarily eliminate tolls on the bond-financed Chicago Skyway and Indiana Toll Road.
O'Bannon mentioned the idea last week when asked about ways to deal with a six-month construction project on the Borman Expressway, according to Phil Bremen, the governor's press secretary.
However, Bremen said Monday that plan will not work because of the bond indenture for debt issued for the Indiana toll road that prohibits tolls from being removed.
Walter Knorr, Chicago's chief financial office, was not available to comment on what such a plan would mean for outstanding Skyway bonds that the city refinanced just last year.
Bremen said another possibility floated by the governor and a northwest Indiana congressman was a federal takeover of the toll roads.
He said both plans at this point do not look "very feasible."
